meta.title: The Mouse Deer and the Crocodiles
meta.textType: story: a traditional tale in an email

paragraphs: On Thursday, June twenty-fifth, the Explorers met in the school library. Leo opened an email from his pen pal, Ravi. Lily and Mia sat next to him. "Read it out loud, Leo," said Mia. "It is a story," said Leo. He began to read.

Dear Leo, my grandma tells me this story when it rains. It is a tale about a mouse deer and some crocodiles. Long ago, a small mouse deer lived among the trees of a jungle. He was hungry, and he was clever. One day, he saw sweet fruit on the other side of a deep river. He wanted the fruit, but the river was full of enormous crocodiles. The mouse deer could not swim, and he was in trouble. Then he had an idea. He stood on the river bank and called to the crocodiles. "The king wants me to count all of you," he said. "Please line up across the river." "Certainly!" said the crocodiles, and they believed him. They lined up immediately, side by side.

Once the crocodiles were in a line, the mouse deer jumped on the first back. "One," he said. He jumped on the second back. One crocodile was looking at the sky when the mouse deer jumped on its back. "Two, three, four," counted the mouse deer. Before they knew it, he was on the last crocodile. Suddenly, he jumped to the other bank. "Thank you for the bridge!" he said. Then he ran to the sweet fruit and ate it. The crocodiles were not happy, but it was too late.
I like this story because the mouse deer is clever. My grandma laughs at the crocodiles every time. Do you have a story like this? Please tell me your story. Best wishes, Ravi. P.S. How is Pip?
text.summary: Leo reads an email from his pen pal Ravi. It tells a tale about a hungry mouse deer who uses a clever idea to cross a river full of crocodiles.
